candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING (7 DAY CHRONIC NOEC)
candidates.exact_span: D. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING (7 DAY CHRONIC NOEC)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether compliance is measured by a 7-day chronic NOEC endpoint (versus another WET protocol or numeric pollutant limit) determines which limit framework applies (A), which monitoring type is required (B), and how non-numeric or missing WET results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall test the effluent for toxicity in accordance with the provisions in this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This mandatory testing language establishes a monitoring obligation for effluent toxicity; interpreting whether it applies unconditionally or only under unstated conditions would change whether WET monitoring was required in FY2025.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D.1 table row APPLICABLE TO FINAL OUTFALL(S)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The outfall scope determines which discharge points are subject to WET monitoring; a different reading of outfall applicability would change which facilities/points are evaluated for monitoring obligations.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D.1 table row CRITICAL DILUTION (%)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Critical dilution defines the effluent concentration at which toxicity compliance is assessed; a different interpretation of the 100% value would change how reported WET results are compared to the applicable limit.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D.1 table row EFFLUENT DILTION SERIES (%)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The dilution series governs how the chronic NOEC is derived from test data; interpreting the series or its use differently could change the computed compliance endpoint used for limit comparison.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D.1 table row TEST SPECIES AND METHODS
candidates.exact_span:
TEST SPECIES AND METHODS           Ceriodaphnia dubia / Method 1002.0
                                      (EPA-821-R-02-013 or latest version)
                                      Pimephales promelas/ Method 1000.0
                                      (EPA/821/R-02/013 or latest version)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which species and EPA methods are required affects both the monitoring obligations that must be met (B) and the methodological basis for determining pass/fail or NOEC-based compliance (A), including ambiguity over whether both species are always required and which document version ('latest version') governs.

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D.1 table row SAMPLE TYPE
candidates.exact_span: SAMPLE TYPE                        Defined in PART I
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sample type is not defined in this segment and is incorporated only by cross-reference to PART I; uncertainty about required sample type (grab vs composite, timing, preservation) could change whether monitoring was properly required or performed (B) and how missing or non-comparable results are classified (C).

candidates.locator: page 8, section part_i, D introductory paragraph
candidates.exact_span: Once initiated, all toxicity tests must be completed unless specific authority has been granted by EPA Region 6 or the State NPDES permitting authority.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a partially conducted or terminated test counts as missing evidence, invalid data, or a documented exception depends on interpreting this completion requirement and the 'specific authority' exception, affecting missing-evidence classification.
